stories.headline: Flávio Bolsonaro lands in Miami after losing Brazil's election
body: The defeated presidential candidate and his family landed at a Miami-area airport on Wednesday.
Brazil's Supreme Court had ordered him to hand over his passports after the vote.
Florida has the largest Brazilian community in the US.
stories.joke: New job title: opposition leader, remote.
stories.vc: A calmer Brazil without a contested result is better news for its currency and stocks.

stories.headline: Russia says Europe won't be at the next Ukraine talks
body: A Kremlin aide said European countries won't join US–Ukraine–Russia talks planned in Abu Dhabi.
Finland's president said Europe would be involved.
Zelenskyy said the talks run from 6 to 10 November in the UAE.
stories.joke: Peace talks where nobody agrees on who's invited. Classic.
stories.vc: Any real progress toward a ceasefire would move energy prices and Europe's defence stocks.

stories.headline: Putin calls Musk a 'genius' as Russia builds its own Starlink
body: Putin praised Elon Musk while comparing Starlink with Russia's planned Rassvet satellite network.
He said Musk has over 5,000 satellites; the real number is estimated at about 10,000.
Russia wants its own satellite internet for its military.
stories.vc: Satellite internet is now a strategic asset; countries want their own, which helps space-tech startups everywhere.

stories.headline: Three of the UK's four nuclear submarines are at sea at once
body: The UK has three Vanguard-class nuclear deterrent submarines at sea at the same time, a first in five years.
Usually at least one is always deployed; the fourth is in maintenance.
It follows a warning from the defence secretary that Britain should be ready for war.
stories.vc: Rising defence alert levels keep European defence budgets, and defence-tech funding, climbing.

stories.headline: Fuel costs end a 'live-aboard' cruise, leaving residents homeless
body: The Odyssey, a ship where people lived while sailing the world, halted its voyage in Cambodia.
Its owner says fuel costs per cabin jumped from about $1,800 a month to $6,000–8,000 during the Iran war.
Hundreds of passengers had to leave their floating homes.
stories.joke: Lifetime at sea, terms and conditions apply.
stories.vc: High fuel prices are breaking business models across travel and shipping.

stories.headline: Ethiopia gets 12 Russian fighter jets and plans S-400 missiles
body: Ethiopia received 12 Su-35 fighter jets from Russia, a year earlier than planned, PM Abiy Ahmed said.
It also plans to buy four S-400 air defence batteries.
Ethiopia is fighting rebels in Tigray and Amhara.
stories.vc: Russia is using arms deals to win influence in Africa, a market Western and Asian suppliers also want.

stories.headline: Canada and the EU meet as Canada eyes 'associate' EU status
body: Canada hosts a summit with the EU in Montreal on 29–30 October.
The EU has proposed making Canada its first 'associate member'.
Talks cover trade, AI, defence, energy and critical minerals as Canada's US ties sour.
stories.joke: Canada, looking for friends who don't threaten tariffs.
stories.vc: Closer Canada–EU ties could redirect trade and investment flows away from the US.

stories.headline: Sensex falls 353 points as IT stocks slide
body: The Sensex closed 353 points lower and the Nifty fell 51 points to 22,698.
At one point the Sensex was down 793 points, with the Nifty IT index off 3.1%.
AWL Agri Business fell 6%.
stories.joke: IT stocks had a bad day. Probably asked an AI for advice.
stories.vc: IT weakness reflects worries about AI eating outsourcing work, a key theme for Indian portfolios.

stories.headline: Meesho's loss shrinks 68% as revenue rises 34%
body: Meesho's September-quarter loss narrowed to ₹132.4 crore from ₹411.4 crore a year earlier.
Operating revenue rose 34% to ₹4,131.6 crore.
The loss was flat versus the June quarter, and its new businesses lost more.
stories.joke: Losing less money: the startup version of a profit.
stories.vc: Investors want proof that value e-commerce can earn money at scale; Meesho is getting closer.

stories.headline: Founder Sanjeev Bikhchandani returns as Info Edge CEO
body: Naukri parent Info Edge says founder Sanjeev Bikhchandani will become MD and group CEO from 3 December.
Hitesh Oberoi steps down after nearly 27 years in an executive role but stays on the board.
Info Edge also reported a Q2 profit of ₹650 crore, up 87%.
stories.vc: Info Edge is a major startup investor (Zomato, PolicyBazaar); its leadership sets the tone for its portfolio.

stories.headline: AI services firm Innodata lays off about 550 in India
body: US-based Innodata reportedly cut nearly 550 jobs in India, about 5% of its global staff.
A termination email blamed the wind-down of a business assignment.
Staff lost system access on 26 October; there were also cuts in the Philippines.
stories.vc: Data-labelling work depends on a few big AI clients; one lost contract can mean hundreds of jobs.

stories.headline: Astrotalk's profit jumps 10x to ₹222 crore
body: Online astrology platform Astrotalk's FY26 profit rose about 10x to ₹222 crore.
Revenue grew 55% to ₹1,823 crore.
International revenue jumped 2.6x and now makes up 34% of sales.
stories.joke: Even the stars didn't see this coming. Or did they?
stories.vc: Profitable consumer niches like this show Indian apps can make money abroad, not just at home.

stories.headline: Bombay High Court says Meta must face ₹1,000 crore suit in India
body: The court rejected Meta's plea to move Blink Digital's ₹1,000 crore suit over disabled ad accounts to California.
It ruled that private contracts can't override Indian law.
The case will now proceed in Mumbai.
stories.joke: Meta's terms said California. The judge said: nice try.
stories.vc: Indian courts asserting jurisdiction over Big Tech changes the legal risk for global platforms here.

stories.headline: Indic AI startups have raised $687M, mostly Sarvam
body: A Tracxn report says 34 companies building AI for Indian languages have raised $687 million in total.
2026 is a record year, with $399 million across nine rounds.
Sarvam alone accounts for more than 80% of all the money.
stories.joke: One startup, most of the cheque book.
stories.vc: Funding is concentrated in one winner; the next wave needs proof that smaller Indic AI players can scale.

stories.headline: Bengaluru plans stricter safety rules for PG accommodations
body: The Greater Bengaluru Authority is drafting new rules for paying-guest (PG) homes.
They cover fire safety, building norms, exits, food hygiene, CCTV and regular audits.
Officials say many PGs barely follow fire rules, and students complain about food.
stories.joke: Finally, someone checks whether the 'homely food' is food.
stories.vc: Stricter rules favour organised co-living brands over small operators, which could speed consolidation.

stories.headline: Anthropic launches tools to show what AI spending buys
body: Anthropic released reports that show managers what their teams made with Claude, what it cost and where work broke down.
It says the data won't be used for training by default.
Its filing shows existing customers' spending grew about 9x in a year.
stories.joke: Finally, a dashboard to justify the AI bill to finance.
stories.vc: Proving ROI is the next battleground for enterprise AI; vendors that show value keep the budget.

stories.headline: Reddit adds a TikTok-style 'For You' feed
body: Reddit users now get a 'For You' feed mixing joined communities with recommended posts.
A separate 'Following' feed shows only communities you've joined.
Reddit hopes it helps people find new communities.
stories.joke: Reddit discovers the algorithm. The comments will be calm about it, surely.
stories.vc: Recommendation feeds lift time spent, and ad revenue, which is why every platform ends up with one.

stories.headline: Hacker leaks data on 40,000+ US Homeland Security staff
body: Names, job titles and contact details of more than 40,000 Homeland Security staff were published online.
They include border and immigration agents and senior officials.
The hacker says the data came from the department's Okta login system.
stories.vc: Identity systems are now prime targets; breaches like this drive spending on login security.
